survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a country governance note describing institutional responsibilities and funding flows in Australia’s adult skills system; it does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC) and therefore does not define a sampling frame, student-level analytic sample, or survey-weight variables. The tables report expenditure shares and governance responsibilities at federal/regional/local levels rather than survey-based estimates requiring complex-survey weights. As a result, there is no weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply, and no replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife) is relevant. For policy interpretation, the key “weighting” analogue is the use of OECD compilation sources and definitions (OECD, 2025[1]) rather than statistical weighting of respondents.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PVs) are generated for cognitive achievement domains in ILSA assessments (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC). This OECD country note does not use any ILSA assessment microdata or cognitive test scores; it summarizes governance structures, stakeholder responsibilities, and expenditure shares across government levels. Missing-data handling is therefore not part of the analysis because there is no respondent-level dataset with item nonresponse or imputation procedures described.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No ILSA student dataset is used. The note compiles governance and expenditure information for Australia from OECD and partner sources (e.g., OECD/UCLG, 2022[2]) and describes responsibilities across federal, state/territory, and local levels.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Australia country note provides an overview of how the adult skills system is governed, focusing on the division of responsibilities across federal (Commonwealth), regional (states and territories), and local levels. It explains that adult education and training for adults is supported through Commonwealth funding transfers to states and territories, while eligibility rules may differ by age due to state/territory discretion. The note describes a combined governance system in which the Australian Government plays roles in funding, policy leadership, and national standards, while states and territories primarily deliver vocational education and training (VET) and related services. It also outlines how national skills strategies are developed jointly (e.g., through the National Skills Agreement and the Skills and Workforce Ministerial Council) and how quality assurance is handled via the Australian Skills Quality Authority. The document reports expenditure structure shares at sub-national levels but does not conduct an assessment-based statistical analysis with benchmarks or model performance metrics.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is not an empirical large-scale assessment analysis paper: it is a governance and institutional mapping note without an ILSA/PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS/PIAAC-style student assessment dataset, outcome variable, or statistical modeling. Consequently, fields required for ML/predictive extraction (e.g., plausible values handling, missing-data strategy, sample sizes, and main findings as model outputs) are either not applicable or not reported by design. The extraction therefore focuses on the policy-relevant descriptive content rather than quantitative model results.
